title: System Usability Scale
instructions: For each statement, mark how strongly you agree or disagree with it, thinking about the learning tool you just used.

items.stem: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
I found the system unnecessarily complex.
I thought the system was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
I found the system very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using the system.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.

scoring.note: Per docs/14 section 2.4: for odd-numbered (positive) items the contribution is r - 1; for even-numbered (negative) items it is 5 - r. Sum the ten contributions and multiply by 2.5 for a 0 to 100 score. Report the single score; do not interpret individual items. Standard SUS wording (Brooke, 1996) retained so scores are comparable with the published distribution; 'system' is not replaced.
